headline: Approved a 60-month trash hauling contract, a $2,383,850 tax-rate reduction, and new ordinances; tabled parking and entrance zoning changes.
summary: Councilors passed changes to the Short-Term Rental Ordinance and to Chapter 2 of the city code. They accepted a $410,037 grant for the 2026-2027 Winter Warming Center and moved several zoning items to the table or to committee.
decisions: Approved Eversource conduit work on Moreland Street.
Approved Eversource conduit work on Clark Street.
Approved Eversource conduit work on Prospect Avenue, with Councilor Scott recused.
Approved and sent for discussion an order asking for a count of one-story MR zoned buildings and possible housing gains.
Approved, as amended, an order for Inspectional Services and Health and Human Services complaint data since January 2026.
Approved a resolution to add artistic features to rotaries, speed bumps and low-visibility areas.
Approved an exception to the firearms ban for air rifle rodent control in Ward 7.
Approved a resolution asking the Director of Mobility to clarify right of way at intersections, including mid-block crossings.
Approved, as amended, a resolution to adopt an Emergency Streets Protocol.
Approved a resolution asking the Director of Finance to collect data on city purchases of AI products.
Approved suspending Rule 2 to move the annual caucus to December 10, 2026.
Laid on the table a zoning amendment to correct parking maximums.
Referred a zoning change removing ground story elevation requirements to the Land Use Committee.
Laid on the table a zoning change clarifying principal entrance requirements.
Laid on the table a zoning change updating terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces.
Approved $100,000 from the Encore fund for Local Cultural Council grants.
Approved a $545,649 budget transfer to correct a Fiscal Year 2027 allocation error.
Approved a 60-month contract with Boston Carting Services LLC for trash, recycling and yard waste hauling.
Approved a $72,824.03 supplemental appropriation for two special elections.
Referred a zoning change on protected accessory dwelling units to the Land Use Committee.
Withdrew Councilor Link's zoning change to Section 3.1.7.c.
Approved the Legislative Matters Committee report on an ordinance detailing prohibitions and exemptions.
Passed an ordinance amending Chapter 2, Article VIII, Division 1 of the city code, 10-1.
Passed amendments to the Short-Term Rental Ordinance, 11-0.
Referred a plan to repeal the medical panel for firefighters and police officers to the Legislative Matters Committee.
Referred the Block 9 Assembly Square housing tax financing agreement to the Finance Committee.
Approved a $92,795 transfer to support the Fiscal Year 2027 Warming Center.
Approved a $69,192 transfer to support the Fiscal Year 2027 Warming Center.
Approved repurposing $69,192 from the COVID-19 Small Business Emergency Stabilization Fund for the Warming Center.
Approved moving $2,383,850 from parking meter receipts to reduce the Fiscal Year 2027 tax rate.
Referred $1,000,000 for the Kennedy Schoolyard renovation to the Finance Committee.
Referred a $1,000,000 transfer to the Community Preservation Act Open Space Reserve to the Finance Committee.
Referred $230,171 for exterior restoration of 277 Broadway to the Finance Committee.
Approved $155,768 from Free Cash to support the Fiscal Year 2027 Warming Center.
Approved a supplemental appropriation of $140,831 for street reconstruction.
Referred $109,000 for a needs assessment of the Somerville Armory to the Finance Committee.
Approved a $46,270 supplemental appropriation for the Hazard Mitigation Plan update.
Referred $45,000 for design of a green space at the Spring Street traffic island to the Finance Committee.
Referred $25,950 in police funds to correct two position grades to the Finance Committee.
Referred a $500,000 federal grant for Union Square Plaza Phase 1 to the Finance Committee.
Referred the confirmation of Lydia Warren as Director of Arts & Culture to a committee.
Approved Fiscal Year 2027 tax classifications, a 175% classification shift and a 35% residential exemption.
Approved accepting a $410,037 grant for the 2026-2027 Winter Warming Center.

Thursday, November 12, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:01 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered recess at 7:09 PM and returned at 7:15 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 8:23 PM and returned at 8:26 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 9:47 PM and returned at 9:57 PM.

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1653 )

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Antonio
- “Tony” Lorusso.

- Councilor Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Michelle
- Neff.

- Councilor McLaughlin requested a moment of silence in memory of 23
- service members who lost their lives since the war in Iran began.

- Councilor Sait requested a moment of silence in memory of Palmina “Ida”
- DeGuglielmo.

## RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Regular Meeting of September 24, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1654 ) RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

3.1. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 25 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1620 ) Moreland Street, from utility pole 263/3 to a point of pickup at 16-18

Moreland Street.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.2. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 9 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1622 ) Clark Street, from utility pole 72/3 to a point of pickup at 26 Clark Street.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

3.3. Grant of Location Eversource applying for a Grant of Location to install 66 feet of conduit in

(ID # 26-1623 ) Prospect Avenue, from the existing Manhole 4121 to a point of pickup at

existing Manhole 25391, next to 47 Webster Avenue.

Councilor Scott recused himself from all discussion of this item.

Jacqui Duffy, representing Eversource, spoke in favor of the item and explained the purpose of the request. There being no further speakers, the Public Hearing was closed.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Order

By Councilor McLaughlin

(ID # 26-1639 ) That the Director of Strategy and Development provide this Council with a

list of how many MR zoned one-story buildings exist, and, if upzoned to six stories, the net increase in housing.

- Councilor McLaughlin explained that he wants to know how many

additional housing units could be created by developing existing one-story buildings and commercial sites that are near public transit.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Housing, Community Development and Equity Committee

4.2. Order

By Councilor McLaughlin and Councilor Sait

(ID # 26-1640 ) That the Director of Constituent Services (311) provide a list of all

Inspectional Services Department related complaints from January 2026 to the present date.

- Councilor McLaughlin referenced a constituent who had to wait for six

months before hearing the results of the inspection for her restaurant, forcing her to delay its opening. Councilor McLaughlin suspects that this may be a

- systemic problem and would like the data to make an informed decision.

- Councilor Wheeler moved to amend this item by adding the “and

Department of Health and Human Services”, so that the Order will read as follows:

- That the Director of Constituent Services (311) provide a list of all
- Inspectional Services Department and Department of Health and Human
- Services related complaints from January 2026 to the present date.

## RESULT: APPROVED AS AMENDED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Public Health and Public Safety Committee

4.3. Resolution

By Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Link and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1641 ) That the Director of Arts and Culture, the Commissioner of Public Works

- and the Director of Infrastructure and Asset Management collaborate to add

artistic features to street rotaries, speed bumps and other areas of low visibility to increase art and traffic safety.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.4. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt, Councilor Scott and Councilor Mbah

(ID # 26-1600 ) Pursuant to section 9-86 of the Code of Ordinances, authorizing Secured

Environments Pest and Wildlife Services to perform air rifle rodent control to mitigate a rodent infestation in Ward 7.

- Councilor Hardt explained that residents in Ward 7 would like to engage

professional marksmen, with specialized equipment, to mitigate a rat infestation. In order to do so, an authorization under Ordinance 9-86 is

needed, since the ordinance has a prohibition against discharging firearms in the city. The company would utilize signage to inform the public of their

- operations and take all necessary precautions to protect the public.

- Legislative and Policy Analyst Brendan Salisbury informed the Council that
- he has spoken to Director of Public Health Colin Zeigler about the request.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Mbah and Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1635 ) That the Director of Mobility clarify design standards as to who has the right

- of way at various intersections across the city, especially mid-block
- crossings where bikers need to connect to the community path.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.6. Resolution

By Councilor Link, Councilor Ewen-Campen and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-1636 ) That the Director of Mobility work with this City Council to adopt the Emergency Streets Protocol.

- Councilor Link explained that this would establish a response to traffic

fatalities whereby immediate, temporary steps would be taken to improve public safety while the city develops any necessary long-term solutions.

- Councilor Wheeler moved to amend the resolution by including the Office
- of Emergency Management. The amendment was approved, as follows:

That the Director of Mobility and the Director of Emergency Management

work with this City Council to adopt the Emergency Streets Protocol.

## RESULT: APPROVED AS AMENDED

4.7. Resolution

By Councilor Link

(ID # 26-1637 ) That the Director of Finance begin collecting data regarding procurement of products or services purchased by the city and that are marketed as artificial intelligence products or purchased specifically for their integrated AI

- features.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.8. Communication By Councilor Wheeler and Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1638 ) Conveying a revision to the notice read at the start of remote Council

meetings.

## RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

4.9. Communication By Councilor Davis

(ID # 26-1656 ) In his capacity as President, requesting that Rule 2 be suspended to move the annual caucus to December 10, 2026.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## RESULT: REFERRED FOR RECOMMENDATION

FOLLOWUP: Land Use Committee

- Councilor Ewen-Campen moved to lay items 5.1 through 5.4 on the table

## RESULT: LAID ON THE TABLE

5.4. Mayor's Request Requesting ordainment of an amendment to Sections 2.1.1, 2.4.5, 3.1.16, (ID # 26-1338 ) 3.2.8, 3.2.9, 3.2.10, 3.2.11, 3.2.15, 4.1.3, 4.1.7, 4.1.8, 4.1.9, 4.1.10, 4.1.13, 4.2.3, 4.2.7, 4.2.8, 4.2.9, 4.2.10, 4.2.13, 4.3.3, 4.3.7, 4.3.8, 4.3.9, 4.3.10, 4.3.13, 4.4.3, 4.4.7, 4.4.8, 4.4.9, 4.4.13, 5.1.3, 5.1.7, 5.1.8, 5.1.9, 5.1.10, 5.1.11, 5.1.14, 6.1.3, 6.1.7, 6.1.8, 6.1.11, 6.2.3, 6.2.7, 6.2.8, 6.2.9, 6.2.12, 6.3.3, 6.3.8, 6.4.3, 6.4.9, 6.4.11, 6.5.3, 6.5.7, 6.5.8, 6.5.11, 7.2.7, 7.2.10, 7.4.3, 7.4.6, 7.4.7, 7.4.8, 7.4.11, 8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.1.4, 8.1.5, 8.1.6, 8.2.2, 8.2.4, 8.2.5, 8.4.16, 8.4.17, 8.4.19, 9.1.7, 12.1.1, 12.1.2, 12.1.4, 12.1.5, 12.1.6, 12.1.7, 12.3.5, 12.3.6, 12.3.7 of the Somerville Zoning Ordinance to update terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces.

- Councilor Ewen-Campen moved to lay items 5.1 through 5.4 on the table

6.C. LAND USE COMMITTEE

6.C.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Land Use, meeting on November 5, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1646 )

- Councilor Ewen-Campen reported that 5 public hearings were held and that

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.D. LEGISLATIVE MATTERS COMMITTEE

6.D.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Legislative Matters, meeting on October 27, (ID # 26-1643 ) 2026.

Councilor Ewen-Campen quoted text from the ordinance that detailed the prohibitions and exemptions contained within it. He addressed the question

of what effect a single local governing body could have by taking this action vs. what the effect would be if none of them did. He spoke about protests

and actions by Immigration and Customs Enforcement and stated that what our government is doing is wrong. Councilor Wheeler commented that

councilors need to make laws that are just. Councilor Mbah noted that the city must align its procurement practices with its values. Councilor Sait

- commented that Israel has been engaging in genocide for 3 years.

- Councilor Strezo asked to sponsor former Alderman Rebecca Gewirtz to

speak on the item, however, Councilor Link objected, triggering a vote under Rule 20 of the City Council’s Rules. Three councilors (Link, Scott

and Sait) voted against allowing Ms. Gewirtz to address the Council, while the remaining eight councilors (Ewen-Campen, Clingan, Strezo, Wheeler, Hardt, McLaughlin, Mbah and Davis) voted to permit her speak on the item.

Ms. Gewirtz began by speaking of her 12-year-old daughter’s perseverance, strength and leadership qualities and how, when her daughter preferred

taking part in an activity at a Somerville gym, she (Ms. Gewirtz) became hesitant about returning to Somerville. Addressing the councilors, she stated that she does not feel welcome in Somerville and that one reason is because of the ordinance being put forth tonight. She asked the councilors what they really know about this conflict and if approving this ordinance is solving

problems for the people in this city. Ms. Gewirtz stated her belief that passage of this ordinance will only add to the fight and lead to higher stakes. She commented that what the council is doing tonight hurts the Jewish

population and she asked that they not be made the scapegoat. She urged the council to vote against this ordinance and to do something hard, as she had to do so many times during her service on the Board of Aldermen, when she

was a minority voice for social justice. She closed by telling councilors that if they don’t want to be like her, they could be like her 12-year-old daughter, a leader, and think for themselves.

- Councilor Strezo commented that Somerville is supposed to be a place

where everyone is welcome. She said that this ordinance uses inaccurate accusations and makes Jewish residents feel unwelcome and fearful. She

maintained that the ordinance is illegal and violates federal procurement practices, while also embodying anti-community. She stated her belief that

all people have right to self-determination in their own homeland and she called the question. President Davis explained that when the question is

- called for, the council has 5 minutes to speak against the motion. Councilor

Link was opposed to the motion because he wished to sponsor a speaker.

- Councilors McLaughlin and Hardt were also opposed to the motion. A a roll
- call vote was taken to close debate and failed with ten councilors against
- (Ewen-Campen, Link, Scott, Clingan, Sait, Wheeler, Hardt, McLaughlin,
- Mbah and Davis) and 1councilor (Strezo) in favor.

- Councilor McLaughlin stated his support for the ordinance, saying that he

took time to meet with both sides of the issue. He stated that Palestinians feel neglected and unheard and noted that the city’s voters have spoken on

the issue. He pointed out that the war in Iran doesn’t get attention in this city although its is affecting everyone through higher gas prices, housing, and inflation costs. Councilor Hardt spoke about crimes against humanity and said that criticizing the actions of the Israeli government should never give license to express hostility towards Jewish people. She feels that the city has a duty to fight antisemitism.

Councilor Link sponsored Jamal Hallal, a resident of Palestinian heritage, who spoke about how he has been treated the past 3 years for saying

Palestinians should have the right to dignity. He spoke about Gaza schools and infrastructure being destroyed and said that the United States sent $25 billion to Israel over the past 3 years. He reminded the council that

Somerville’s electorate has voted to take tax dollars out of this fight and he urged councilors to pass this ordinance as written.

Councilor Scott made a motion to approve the item.
